:::{#def-quantifier}
#### Quantifier

A **quantifier** turns a predicate $P(x)$ (@def-predicate)
about the elements $x$ of a set $S$ into a proposition (@def-proposition).
There are two: the universal quantifier (@def-universal-quantifier)
and the existential quantifier (@def-existential-quantifier).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-universal-quantifier}
#### Universal quantifier

The **universal quantifier** "for all" is a quantifier (@def-quantifier):
$\forall x \in S, P(x)$ ("for every $x$ in $S$, $P(x)$")
is true when $P(x)$ is true for every element $x$ of $S$,
and false otherwise.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-existential-quantifier}
#### Existential quantifier

The **existential quantifier** "there exists" is a quantifier (@def-quantifier):
$\exists x \in S, P(x)$ ("there is an $x$ in $S$ such that $P(x)$")
is true when $P(x)$ is true for at least one element $x$ of $S$,
and false otherwise.

:::
